To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the composition of, or precursor incorporation into, a number of brain polypeptides change during development and that the changes in composition and precursor incorporation are not always parallel.
The composition of polypeptide species of rat brain slices changes with age and that these changes are not accompanied by parallel changes in precursor uptake.

the polypeptide composition of rat brain slices undergoes major developmental changes between 15 and 60 days postnatal and that the changes in precursor incorporation into polypeptides are not parallel to the changes in relative amount of the polypeptides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the developmental changes in polypeptide composition of brain slices.
the development of the brain and its constituent cell types, in particular the oligodendrocyte and myelin sheaths.
the study of developmental changes in the polypeptide composition of the rat brain, using SDS-PAGE coupled with fluorography of polypeptides labelled in vitro with L-[3, 4(n)-3 H]valine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polypeptides of brain slices undergo developmental changes in both composition and precursor incorporation.
the developmental increases in polypeptides were not accompanied by increases in precursor incorporation and vice versa.
there are developmental changes in polypeptide composition, precursor incorporation and localisation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the changes in relative amount and precursor incorporation into polypeptides of brain slices during postnatal development are not simply a consequence of the changes in protein content and precursor incorporation of the slices as a whole, but are the consequence of changes in the relative rates of synthesis and degradation of individual polypeptides.

there are at least 17 polypeptides in the rat brain slice polyeptide profile, and that the developmental changes in these polypeptides can be divided into two groups: (a) polypeptides whose developmental changes in relative amount and precursor incorporation are parallel, and (b) polypeptides which show developmental decreases in precursor incorporation but little change in amount.
developmental changes in polypeptide synthesis and turnover are accompanied by changes in polypeptides which are associated with myelin and mitochondria.
